newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin op diverts investors from Russian shares.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin op diverts investors from Russian shares.

text.p: Leading Russian shares closed mixed on Friday as Western investors abstained from buying before President Boris Yeltsin heart operation, which could be held any day now, traders said.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares rose by 0.37 percent to 178.64 on $14.25 million in volume.
"There is no interest in Russian shares now," said Alexei Goncharov, chief analyst from Russian Brokerage House. "Foreign investors are abstaining from buying before Yeltsin's operation."
Presidential spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said on Friday that the date for president's operation could be set any time.

"Everyone is very nervous," said Oleg Dobritsky, chief trader from IK OLMA. "Everyone is following political news closely. Market participants do not want to change their positions seriously before political news come."
Traders said that if the operation date is not announced beforehand, the market nervousness would lead to more fluctuations on the market.
Goncharov said a fall in American Depositary Receipts of Russian companies led to a fall in their shares on the Russian market as the operation nears.
"I can feel people do not want to buy," he said.

Chelyabenergo rose to $0.125 from $0.11 at Thursday's close, Tatneft was up to $39.00 from $37.25, Norilsk Nickel fell to $6.3 from $6.68, Mosenergo edged up to $0.953 from $0.955 and UES was traded at $0.0814 after $0.0817.
